items.question: What exalted status belongs to a teacher who has mastered control?
premises: A teacher becomes fully self-controlled
Such a teacher commands supreme reverence
Even the gods bow down to him
items.inference: A self-controlled teacher is worthy of homage even from the gods.
uncertainties: vaśī bhūto may imply control over senses or over others; context favors self-mastery
items.plain_english: Even the gods bow down to that teacher who has become fully self-controlled.

rows.grounds: vocative or part of compound context

items.question: What spiritual destination is attained by one who drinks nectar with proper inner state?
premises: One may drink nectar with a particular inner state
Such drinking is linked to a higher attainment
The result is reaching the goddess's city
items.inference: Drinking nectar with the proper inner state leads one to the goddess's city.
uncertainties: amṛta bhavena may mean with an attitude of immortality or with ritual nectar; both are possible
items.plain_english: O Goddess, whoever drinks the nectar with that inner state should go to the city of the Goddess.

items.question: Is any expiation required in that state even when established in Vedic observance?
premises: The context concerns a specific elevated state
Vedic standing is acknowledged
No expiation applies there
items.inference: In that state, no expiation is required, even for one established in the Veda.
uncertainties: tatra refers back to the prior state or attainment; exact antecedent depends on preceding context
items.plain_english: For in that state there is no expiation at all, even for one established in the Veda.

items.question: How may one's own doctrine be aligned with Vedic and Mahārudra teachings?
premises: An alternative approach is presented
One's own view can be considered
It may be understood in accordance with the Vedas and Mahārudra's word
items.inference: One's own doctrine may be upheld as consistent with the Vedas and the word of Mahārudra.
uncertainties: syntactic relation is compressed; exact predicate is implied rather than explicit
items.plain_english: Or else, one's own view is to be understood in accordance with the Vedas, as in the word of Mahārudra.

items.question: What is the proper non-dual understanding of deity, sovereignty, and relation with the teacher?
premises: Non-duality is affirmed
The sovereignty of the deity is affirmed
Duality is denied in relation with the teacher
items.inference: Deity and its sovereignty are non-dual, and there is no duality with the teacher.
uncertainties: legacy hint for dvaitaṃ as non-duality appears erroneous; glossed as duality based on nā dvaitaṃ
items.plain_english: Non-duality is the sovereignty of the deity; there is no duality together with the teacher.

items.question: In what supreme forms is the teacher identified for the devoted disciple?
premises: The teacher is declared to be the refuge
The teacher is identified as god
The teacher is identified as goddess
items.inference: The teacher is the ultimate refuge and is identical with both god and goddess.
uncertainties: repetition of guruḥ devo may be emphatic or textual doubling; preserved as given
items.plain_english: O beloved, the teacher is the refuge, the teacher is god, the teacher is god, and the teacher is likewise the goddess.

rows.grounds: second member of compound, sandhi form
final member of compound, sandhi form

items.question: Does the teacher remain the sole refuge regardless of apparent learning or limitation?
premises: The teacher may appear to know little
The teacher may appear to know much
In all cases the teacher is the refuge
items.inference: Whether seemingly of little or great knowledge, the teacher alone is always the refuge.
items.plain_english: Whether of little knowledge or of vast knowledge, the teacher alone is always the refuge.

items.question: What is the true status of the teacher's wife in relation to the teacher?
premises: The teacher's wife is addressed in this teaching
She is identified with the teacher
No doubt is permitted regarding this
items.inference: The teacher's wife is none other than the teacher himself, without doubt.
items.plain_english: O Great Goddess, the teacher's wife is the teacher alone; there is no doubt.

rows.grounds: gerundive, object or subject of obligation

items.question: What consequence follows if one hesitates or reacts wrongly to what must be eaten?
premises: What is given is to be eaten without doubt
A negative reaction or alteration is possible
Such reaction leads to a downward course
items.inference: One must eat without doubt, for aversion or alteration leads to a downward fall.
uncertainties: bhojanīyaṃ likely refers to food offered by or associated with the guru; antecedent implied
items.plain_english: It is to be eaten without doubt; if there is aversion or alteration, the result is a downward course.

items.question: What ritual and spiritual purity is attributed to the teacher's remnants?
premises: The teacher's remnants are discussed
They are declared greatly pure
They are said to be supreme beyond the supreme
items.inference: The teacher's remnants are supremely pure, surpassing even the highest purity.
items.plain_english: The teacher's remnants are likewise declared to be greatly pure, supreme beyond the supreme.

rows.grounds: second member of compound, locative sense

items.question: What long-term dwelling near the teacher is presented as an ideal condition?
premises: Dwelling near the teacher is considered
A duration of fifty years is specified
The dwelling is in an excellent setting
items.inference: Living near the teacher for fifty years in an excellent state is set forth as an ideal.
uncertainties: uttame may qualify antike or the manner of dwelling; taken as excellent condition
items.plain_english: If one should dwell near the teacher for fifty years in an excellent state...

rows.grounds: second member of compound, sandhi form
second member of compound, sandhi form

items.question: What final attainment follows a life of excellent enjoyments in this world?
premises: One enjoys excellent pleasures in this world
This life comes to an end
One becomes an attendant of the goddess or the god
items.inference: After enjoying excellent pleasures here, one becomes an attendant in the retinue of the goddess or the god.
uncertainties: devī gaṇo deva gaṇo may indicate alternative or combined attainment
items.plain_english: Having enjoyed excellent pleasures here, in the end one should become an attendant of the goddess or an attendant of the god.

items.question: For how long does the accomplished hero continue to roam freely?
premises: The subject is described as a hero
He roams freely
His roaming lasts as long as moon, sun, and stars endure
items.inference: The hero roams freely for as long as the moon, sun, and stars exist.
items.plain_english: That hero roams freely as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

items.question: What reverence is owed to the teacher's son or daughter according to proper rule?
premises: The teacher's son or daughter is the object of respect
Bowing to them is prescribed
This should be done according to proper rule
items.inference: One should bow to the teacher's son or daughter in accordance with the prescribed rule.
uncertainties: tat functions as genitive equivalent in this context
items.plain_english: One should bow to his son or his daughter in accordance with the proper rule.

rows.grounds: relative locative, sandhi form of yatra

items.question: How should one orient oneself daily toward the direction of the teacher's abode?
premises: The teacher's place lies in some direction
Daily morning practice is indicated
One should face that direction
items.inference: One should always face the direction of the teacher's abode, especially in the morning.
items.plain_english: In whichever direction the teacher's place lies, one should always face that direction, especially in the morning.

rows.grounds: locative adverb, sandhi fragment of atra

items.question: What spiritual accomplishment results from bowing with devotion toward the teacher's direction?
premises: One bows endowed with devotion
Such devotion is directed toward the teacher
The practitioner becomes accomplished
items.inference: One who bows with devotion becomes accomplished, without doubt.
uncertainties: nā tra reflects sandhi for na atra; analyzed as given fused form
items.plain_english: Endowed with devotion, one should bow; he becomes accomplished—there is no doubt here.

items.question: How are the trees and creepers in the teacher's domain regarded in sacred terms?
premises: Rows of trees are present in the teacher's domain
Creepers are also present
They are regarded as wish-fulfilling
items.inference: The rows of trees and creepers there are to be regarded as wish-fulfilling.
uncertainties: syntactic compression leaves implied location (guru's place) from context
items.plain_english: The rows of trees are rows of wish-fulfilling trees, and the creepers are remembered as wish-fulfilling creepers.

items.question: What divine identity is attributed to the maidservants dwelling in the teacher's house?
premises: Maidservants dwell in the teacher's house
They are given a sacred identification
They are proclaimed to be Bhairavīs
items.inference: The maidservants in the teacher's house are proclaimed to be Bhairavīs.
items.plain_english: The maidservants situated in the teacher's house are proclaimed to be Bhairavīs.

items.question: What cosmic merit is gained by performing circumambulation in this sacred context?
premises: Circumambulation is performed by someone
The act has a vast equivalent merit

items.inference: By that circumambulation, one is deemed to have circumambulated the entire seven-island earth.
uncertainties: object of circumambulation is implied from prior context, likely the guru or guru's abode
items.plain_english: By him, circumambulation is made of the earth with its seven islands.

rows.grounds: ablative of comparison, sandhi form of tvattaḥ

items.question: How does the declared greatness of the teacher compare even to the goddess addressed?
premises: The goddess is addressed as the speaker's counterpart
The teacher is compared to her
The teacher is declared even greater than her
items.inference: The teacher is declared by you to be even greater than you.
uncertainties: speaker attribution depends on dialogue context; tvayā indicates the addressed deity declares this
items.plain_english: This teacher has been declared by you to be even greater than you.

items.question: What supreme authority does the teacher hold in relation to all mantras?
premises: The teacher is the subject of affirmation
All mantras are within scope
The teacher is declared supreme in that domain
items.inference: The teacher alone is supreme in relation to all mantras.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, lord of gods, that very teacher is now supreme in all mantras.

rows.grounds: locative adverb, sandhi fragment of atra

items.question: Does the teacher's supreme status extend across different tantric traditions without exception?
premises: The great Śaiva tradition is included
The Saura tradition is included
The same teacher is affirmed in both
items.inference: The teacher holds the same supreme status in both the great Śaiva and Saura traditions, without doubt.
uncertainties: na tra reflects sandhi for na atra; analyzed as given fused form
items.plain_english: In the great Śaiva and in the Saura traditions, he is the teacher—there is no doubt here.

items.question: What human appearance does the teacher assume at the time of mantra transmission?
premises: The context is the time of giving mantra
The setting involves a human recipient or form
The teacher appears as human
items.inference: At the time of mantra transmission, the teacher appears in human form.
uncertainties: mānuṣe may refer to a human disciple or human context; taken as human setting
items.plain_english: O daughter of the mountain, at the time of giving mantra, in the human realm, the teacher is indeed human.

rows.grounds: locative adverb, sandhi fragment of atra

items.question: Is the teacher's essential status merely human despite appearing in human form?
premises: The teacher appears in a human context
The state of being teacher is considered
That state is not merely human
items.inference: Therefore, although appearing in human form, the teacher's true status is not merely human, without doubt.
uncertainties: na na tra reflects emphatic negation and sandhi for na atra; analyzed as given fused forms
items.plain_english: Therefore, O Goddess, in the human realm the state of being teacher is not merely human—there is no doubt here.
